title: decision: the framed_content_tbs_hash check needs the GroupContext, like the signature
description:
Mark 2026-11-26: guess the Right Thing and go with it. Item 2 of bead
mimid-1wgh.44.22, which is held for posting to the author.

## The ambiguity

semiprivatemessage-08 §3.3 L379-385, for an external receiver:

  It verifies the padding consists of the appropriate number of zero
  bytes, and verifies that the framed_content_tbs_hash is correct. If
  the external receiver has a copy of the GroupContext, it verifies that
  the signature in the FramedContentAuthData is valid.

So the hash check is unconditional and the signature check is
conditional on holding the GroupContext. But FramedContentTBS embeds the
GroupContext for a member sender (RFC 9420 §6.1), so
hash(FramedContentTBS) cannot be computed without it either. As written
the first sentence asks for something the second sentence says you may
not be able to do.

## Chosen: both checks are conditional on the GroupContext

The only self-consistent reading. A receiver without the GroupContext
can decrypt the content and check the padding, and can do neither hash
nor signature; a receiver with it does all four.

Taking the sentence literally instead -- hash always, signature
sometimes -- would mean either that FramedContentTBS is to be hashed
without its GroupContext, which is not the structure RFC 9420 §6.1
defines, or that an external receiver must always hold the GroupContext,
which would make the signature sentence's condition dead text.

## What mimid does

The hub holds group_info and the ratchet tree per room (`NewEvent`), so
it can reconstruct the GroupContext and is never the receiver without
one. mimid therefore checks both the hash and the signature, always, and
a failure of either is a refusal and not a warning: §3.3's hash is the
whole mechanism that stops a sender encrypting one thing to the group
and another to the hub, so a hub that skipped it would hold content the
members never agreed to.

The conditional path is implemented and tested anyway, because the type
is public and a caller that is not the hub may have no GroupContext.

## Still to put to the author

Bead mimid-1wgh.44.22 item 2 stays open: §3.3 should make the hash check
conditional in the same breath as the signature, or say that an external
receiver MUST hold the GroupContext and drop the condition from the
signature. Either fixes it; the current text cannot be followed as
written.
